title: Midday Resource Triage Notebook
content:
Quick context:
- Midday spot check after the morning burst: two queues spiking (image-preproc, chat-rerank), intermittent OOMs on rtx-pool-7. Not yet customer-impacting but trending up.

Immediate checklist (do these in order):
1) Verify cluster autoscaler state
   - kubectl -n infra get hpa,deploy -o wide | grep autoscaler
   - Check prometheus: infra.autoscaler.scale_events (last 15m)
2) Inspect GPU nodes with recent evictions
   - kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-rtx -o wide
   - ssh node-rtx-7 -> sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since "3h" | grep -i oom
   - nvidia-smi dmon -s u  (watch per-process mem)
3) Rebalance low-util pools to free slots for high-priority jobs
   - drain low-util nodes (cordon + evict noncritical pods)
   - patch deploys: set podPriority for rerank to high-priority if SLA-critical
4) Network egress check (noticed retries on external image fetch)
   - curl -I https://edge-cache.redwood/api/health from a problematic pod
   - Check egress-NAT gw logs for 10.44.0.0/16

Observations / debugging notes:
- rtx-pool-7 showing 14% sustained mem spikes driven by a long-lived attention cache process (candidate: legacy reranker).
- Autoscaler did 2 scale-ups at 09:12 and 09:47 then tripped back down quickly; investigate scaler cooldown/tuning.
- Network: sporadic 502s when pulling from edge-cache; likely transient upstream, but coincides with pod restarts.

Short-term mitigations (today):
- Add a temporary 10% buffer to gpu-reserved in pool config (apply via kustomize patch w/ rollout pause). Owner: Samir. ETA: 2h.
- Force restart of legacy-reranker job on rtx-pool-7 to clear attention cache (non-destructive restart). Owner: me. ETA: 15m.
- Increase autoscaler min replicas by 1 for burst window (09:00-18:00) while we monitor. Owner: Noah. ETA: 30m.

Longer-term action items (add to backlog):
- Audit long-lived attention-cache processes across models; propose a TTL or checkpoint strategy. (JIRA-PLT-4821)
- Add an alert for "gpu-per-node memory tail" (95th p90 mem per node persist > 80% for 10m).
- Investigate pulling edge-cache behind a regional HTTP cache to reduce egress spikes.

Notes to self / gotchas:
- When restarting legacy-reranker, ensure model version pinning is kept (we hit an incident last quarter by rolling to v2-beta).
- Autoscaler cooldown defaults are aggressive; set annotation autoscaler.k8s.io/cooldown: 120s for tested pools.
- Do not cordon nodes with active jobs tagged customer-critical unless fallback routing verified.

Small capacity table (back-of-envelope):
- rtx-pool-7: 8 nodes x 48GB = 384 GB total; current in-use ~330GB -> free ~54GB (but fragmentation means usable ~30GB)
- expected burst req for rerank queue: 3x 6GB jobs => 18GB temporary
- actionable: adding 1 node (48GB) clears burst and gives buffer.

Scratch commands I ran / to run:
- kubectl -n infra describe hpa autoscaler-rerank | sed -n '1,120p'
- kubectl get pods -n jobs -l app=legacy-reranker -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'
- ssh node-rtx-7 sudo docker ps --format '{{.Names}} {{.Status}}'

Open questions / escalate if no fix in 90m:
- If autoscaler misbehaves on scale-down, escalate to infra-sre (page: @oncall-sre).
- If network 502s persist after clearing local cache, open a ticket with CDN provider and route through edge-cache fallback.

End-of-shift handoff (if I step out):
- What I did: restarted legacy-reranker on rtx-pool-7, added temporary gpu-reserved buffer config (patch id: patch-rtx-buf-0313), left autoscaler min+1.
- What to watch: pods in jobs namespace for repeated OOMs, infra.autoscaler.scale_events metric, egress 502 rate.

Other random notes / TODO:
- Add a short doc on "how we choose which pool to steal from during bursts" (link to product routing policy).
- Sync with model-ops about quantization suggestions for reranker to reduce mem by ~30%.

-- amina
